paragraphs.text: This leaf comes from [Anhua](anhua:where-it-is), a mountain county on the middle stretch of the Zi river, at the northern foot of the Xuefeng mountains in central northern Hunan. It is a country of hills and steep valleys where rice is hard to grow and tea does well. The county is counted as the main home of [Anhua dark tea](anhua-dark:definition), a protected origin product tied to this ground. That tie is also about the air: the same warm, wet climate that grows the leaf is the one it is piled and kept in, which is [why the trade links the finished tea to the place](anhua:why-people-value-it) and not only to the method.

It was made in 2023, so it is three years old. Anhua tea is [kept for years](anhua-dark:ageing) and is expected to change as it rests, but the trade sets no count of years at which it becomes aged. It asks for a clean, dry, aired place, away from mould and other smells.

Like every Anhua tea, it begins as [heimaocha](anhua-dark:making), the raw tea made from large local leaf: fixed, rolled, piled, rolled again and dried over a wood fire, which in Anhua burns pine. As a [dark tea](dark:definition), its leaf is left to change in warmth and moisture after it is made, and microbes and the leaf's own chemistry slowly darken it. This one stays loose, not pressed into a brick or a roll.

brewing.text: In a small pot or gaiwan, use water at the boil and start with a steep of about 15 to 30 seconds, a little longer each round. Pressed and aged Anhua tea is also commonly simmered in a pot.

notice.text: Pine smoke or pine resin above all, a sweet taste and aftertaste, and a mellow, thick, smooth cup; a liquor from yellow and orange to orange-red. Young tea is often smokier in the first infusions and a little bitter, sweetening as the infusions go on.
